note: Shit My Sponsor Says: 200 lines. shitmysponsorsays posts ten to start, then two days on and one day off at 7am Eastern, on the yellow legal pad card, in this order, until they run out (supabase/functions/porch-daily). Add new ones at the END.
items: “You want advice, or do you need a getaway driver with a sober date?”
“You’ve tried everything except listening. Apparently that’s the premium package.”
“Your best thinking has a body count of friendships. Let somebody else drive.”
“You saying ‘I got this’ is why I keep my ringer on.”
“You’re not confused. You’re pissed the bullshit didn’t get approved.”
“Seven people told you no. This isn’t a focus group, dumbass.”
“You’ll go to any lengths except across town, before noon, or without air-conditioning.”
“That resentment’s been living in your head so long it’s claiming you as a dependent.”
“You want closure? Close the damn app. There’s a button.”
“You skimmed the steps like the side effects on something you already swallowed.”
“Your program has the commitment level of a hotel Wi-Fi agreement.”
“God said no. I’m not the appeals court for your dumb shit.”
“You hired help and immediately tried to become management. There’s your problem.”
“Your head’s full of breaking news from an unreliable damn source.”
“That story’s so polished I can see your bullshit in it.”
“Your apology had more exclusions than flood insurance.”
“You said ‘protecting my peace’ while actively ruining six people's afternoons.”
“Congratulations on being right. Who’s still taking your calls?”
“I’m not cosigning that idea. Your judgment’s already in collections.”
“Everybody else gets a documentary. Your part gets witness protection.”
“Your gut has terrible references and you keep rehiring it.”
“You’re thirty days sober and inspecting the place like you own the damn building.”
“Fire me after you follow a suggestion. Otherwise we’re ending an internship you never started.”
“You called for advice and brought a rebuttal. Next time debate the toaster.”
“I love you. Your bullshit has not earned the same arrangement.”
“You don’t need another bottom. You need to stop treating this one like a timeshare.”
“A rough patch? You’ve installed cable and registered to vote there.”
“You keep inviting chaos over and acting shocked it drinks out of the carton.”
“That loophole’s just your last disaster with a fake mustache.”
“This wasn’t an accident. You sent calendar invites.”
“Out of nowhere? Your dumb shit left a forwarding address.”
“You spent a week campaigning for this decision. Own the election results.”
“Your recovery plan requires seven other people to get their shit together first. Brilliant.”
“You want personal growth with a guarantee that nothing personal changes.”
“I said ‘think about it.’ You heard ‘break ground Monday.’”
“You ignored every warning and now you want a personalized damn prophecy.”
“A fresh start with the same bullshit? That’s a rerun in a new apartment.”
“You’ve got contingency plans for everything except common sense.”
“You need somebody who doesn’t know you to approve this. Try airport strangers.”
“You’re asking permission from the parking lot. The horse has already Ubered out.”
“A detailed explanation doesn’t turn a dumb decision into a graduate thesis.”
“One more retelling and you’ll have rescued everybody from the mess you made.”
“Your memory has a suspiciously generous employee discount for you.”
“You’re financing the truth over thirty-six monthly admissions.”
“Every time you say ‘technically,’ an honest detail leaves the room.”
“What happened? Save the legal defense for whoever you owe money.”
“Your honesty has more passwords than your damn bank account.”
“You’re protecting their feelings? Funny how your ass keeps getting the protection.”
“You left out one detail. Apparently it was the load-bearing one.”
“Your part’s so small in this version it qualifies for a travel bottle.”
“You’ve convinced yourself. Unfortunately, that’s the easiest sale in town.”
“You said ‘long story short’ forty minutes ago. File a missing-person report for short.”
“Nobody got the truth, but you didn’t lie. Hell of a magic trick.”
“Stop giving me bonus features. Play the damn scene where you did it.”
“Your excuse requires more assembly than a backyard shed.”
“You said ‘honestly’ like we just upgraded the call.”
“You buried the important detail so deep it needs a mining permit.”
“You don’t need a better explanation. You need to retire three of them.”
“The truth doesn’t have to make you employee of the month.”
“If a question wrecks your story, the question isn’t the problem.”
“Your fourth step reads like a lawsuit written by somebody banned from the courthouse.”
“You’ve inventoried everyone’s defects except the asshole holding the pen.”
“Your part was ‘loving too hard’? Interesting name for reading their messages.”
“You’re writing an inventory with the enthusiasm of somebody hiding assets.”
“Yes, they’re an asshole. This assignment is about the one I’m talking to.”
“We’re looking for your patterns. You keep submitting suspects.”
“Being too nice wasn’t the defect. Sending the invoice afterward was.”
“You’ve written nineteen pages about them and one comma about you.”
“You’re doing a fearless inventory with a damn redaction marker.”
“This is a fifth step. The Academy isn’t voting on your suffering.”
“You don’t need to dramatize the inventory. The facts have already called security.”
“Enough detail that I don’t need a decoder ring and two witnesses.”
“You can’t skip the embarrassing part. That’s the damn address we came to.”
“Your defects aren’t family heirlooms. Quit polishing them.”
“You’re ready for God to remove everybody else’s shortcomings. Very generous of you.”
“You surrendered, then attached a rider demanding creative control.”
“Identifying your defect doesn’t give you a license to keep being an ass.”
“You call it ‘just how I am’ like it came with a federal protection order.”
“Nobody’s removing your personality. We’re trying to stop it from collecting complaints.”
“Your willingness has been ‘coming soon’ longer than the damn road construction.”
“Your amends list keeps shrinking. Are people getting pardoned while I sleep?”
“That apology turned into a countersuit before you finished breathing.”
“You apologized and then repossessed every word.”
“Everything after ‘but’ is you trying to get your deposit back.”
“You hurt them and assigned them reading. Who the hell runs that school?”
“You want forgiveness by Friday. Should they overnight it?”
“You don’t get to leave a one-star review of how they received your amends.”
“They didn’t hug you? You confessed, dumbass. You didn’t win a raffle.”
“You paid back your own debt and want a parade. I’ll notify the marching band.”
“A living amends means the bullshit stops living there.”
“You’re using apologies like a monthly subscription to the same bad behavior.”
“Your ‘sorry’ has more repeat customers than a tire shop. Fix something.”
“Your apology doesn’t need a soundtrack. They’ve already heard your greatest hits.”
“You’re explaining the harm like you want a coupon applied at checkout.”
“Make the amends. Nobody ordered a TED Talk from the defendant.”
“They know you were struggling. They were financing the damn experience.”
“You want painless amends? Should’ve tried harmless behavior.”
“You’re sincere until somebody declines to make you feel better about it.”
“Forgiveness isn’t a receipt you wave at the next complaint.”
“You drafted the redemption post before paying them back. Beautiful priorities.”
“Your resentment has a guest room. Your actual friends have to make appointments.”
“You’ve won that imaginary argument six hundred times. Still no damn trophy.”
“They ruined ten minutes. You expanded the contract to cover the fiscal year.”
“You’re stalking their happiness to check whether yours has recovered. Sound system.”
“Your car’s falling apart, but that grudge gets premium maintenance.”
“You don’t like them? Fine. Cancel the damn surveillance operation.”
“That paragraph isn’t communication. It’s an emotional hostage note with punctuation.”
“You’ve outsourced your sleep to somebody who doesn’t know they’re on payroll.”
“Your resentment’s old enough to have a pension. Let the bastard retire.”
“You migrated the screenshots to your new phone. That’s commitment to being pissed.”
“You’re keeping a scoreboard for people who left the stadium years ago.”
“You’re letting it go? Then why does it have a damn newsletter?”
“They’ve moved on. You’re still hosting the reunion special.”
“You’ve made one bad afternoon into a recurring calendar event.”
“You don’t have to bless them. Just stop writing speeches in the shower.”
“You’re asking for peace while charging the damn flamethrower.”
“Your grudge shows up early and stays late. Hire it for the coffee commitment.”
“You’ve refined that insult for a month. Shame you won’t work that hard on an apology.”
“You want them out of your head, but you keep providing fresh towels.”
“You’re standing on principle. Looks a hell of a lot like sitting in spite.”
“Twelve meetings and your closest relationship is with the creamer.”
“You hate how the meeting’s run? Grab a chair. It’s the one you fold.”
“You arrive for the middle and leave before the end. Hell of a commitment to excerpts.”
“You want a warm welcome with your earbuds in. Should we send a damn push notification?”
“You’re reviewing meetings like restaurants and tipping nobody.”
“You know which chair squeaks, but you can’t name the guy beside you.”
“Nobody understands you? You’ve given us ‘fine’ for eight consecutive weeks.”
“Wrap it up. Your childhood has used the room’s entire rental agreement.”
“Hell of a share. Any plans to become that guy outside this room?”
“You’ve got one more point? Put it in next week’s damn budget.”
“You’re chairing a meeting. Nobody’s waiting for your opening monologue.”
“You need a service position to help? The trash isn’t checking credentials.”
“You’re waiting for a spiritual calling to plug in a coffeepot.”
“You want applause for service? Volunteer at a theater.”
“You’ve given that newcomer eleven instructions and still don’t know his damn name.”
“You’re policing the readings with a book that’s never escaped its shrink-wrap.”
“Try listening without loading your next round of bullshit.”
“You want a meeting with no annoying people. Stay home and see how long that lasts.”
“You’ve turned fellowship into a talent show nobody agreed to enter.”
“Forty meeting apps and zero meetings. Hell of a digital sobriety collection.”
“You want a partner or somebody to babysit the silence in your apartment?”
“Ten days and you’re picking curtains. You haven’t even seen them handle a flat tire.”
“If you need sponsor approval to text your ex, you already know the damn answer.”
“You call it chemistry. Your bank calls it suspicious activity.”
“You say you want stability, then complain nobody’s making your stomach hurt.”
“You’re dating who they could become. The person who showed up is cashing the checks.”
“Those red flags aren’t decorations, dumbass.”
“Taking it slow? Your toothbrush already has squatters’ rights.”
“You’re doing unpaid overtime for a relationship that never hired you.”
“Missing them doesn’t require reopening a business that damn near bankrupted you.”
“You want honesty, but you’re pretending you’re fine with the casual thing.”
“Refreshing the screen isn’t foreplay. Put the phone down.”
“Ask them what they meant. I sponsor you; I don’t decrypt flirting.”
“You’re auditioning against an ex who isn’t even in the damn room.”
“Three dates and joint checking? At least learn their last name before the overdraft.”
“They answered at midnight. So does the gas station. Calm down.”
“Your breakup doesn’t need a press secretary and a public comment period.”
“Your boundary disappears every Friday like it’s paid hourly.”
“You blocked them and built a viewing platform. Very decisive.”
“Your love life requires more emergency coverage than a damn hospital.”
“You prayed for patience and threatened the printer. Productive morning.”
“You’ve made God an employee and you’re disappointed in the performance review.”
“You’re furious you can’t meditate peacefully. Read that sentence back.”
“Use your regular voice. God’s already heard you in traffic.”
“You want enlightenment delivered same-day with free returns.”
“You’re searching for a cosmic message. Your landlord’s left three.”
“You turned five minutes of silence into a competitive damn sport.”
“You surrendered with more conditions than a hostage negotiation.”
“Your gratitude list is a roast of people doing worse than you.”
“You thanked God and called somebody an asshole before ‘amen.’ Efficient.”
“You’re exploring the meaning of existence while abandoning the shopping cart diagonally.”
“You want divine guidance for dishes. Hot water’s a promising start.”
“You’ll accept reality as soon as reality submits the changes you requested.”
“Your serenity lasted until somebody used your mug. Deep roots.”
“You want humility, but only if people notice you getting it.”
“You photographed your gratitude and forgot to thank the person who helped.”
“You don’t need a retreat in the mountains. You need to stop arguing in the kitchen.”
“You’ve researched prayer longer than you’ve tried it. Hell of a literature review.”
“Your inner peace went down with the router. Call tech support before declaring a spiritual crisis.”
“You want God to think exactly like you. We’re trying to diversify management.”
“You skipped lunch and now everybody’s an asshole. Have a sandwich before sentencing.”
“Four hours of sleep and you’re announcing the collapse of civilization. Take a damn nap.”
“You’re mapping your destiny on sheets that could stand up by themselves.”
“You’ve built a committee around a task that takes ten minutes.”
“You’re buying self-care with the money you owe somebody. Nice spa package.”
“You bought a fourth planner. Apparently the first three couldn’t schedule a personality change.”
“You want less stress but keep accepting invitations like you’re collecting air miles.”
“You saw a disaster and asked if they needed an assistant manager.”
“You can ignore a call without issuing a declaration of independence.”
“You wrote a three-paragraph post about the dishes. Soap would’ve been quicker.”
“You need motivation to get dressed? Your pants aren’t proposing marriage.”
“You’re solving hypothetical problems to avoid the real one blinking on the counter.”
“Your emergency has been trying to reach you since Tuesday.”
“You’ve meant well so long your intentions qualify for retirement benefits.”
“You’re waiting for the perfect moment. It heard your excuses and blocked you.”
“You had a bad afternoon and drafted an obituary for your entire future.”
“You want a whole new life? Finish the damn email in the old one.”
“You can explain the task for an hour or do it in five minutes. Tough little puzzle.”
“Call me before you make the mess. I’m tired of getting cast in the cleanup crew.”
“I’m proud of you, you stubborn bastard. Try accepting one nice thing without cross-examining it.”
